correctness.rationale: For a complete multipartite graph, a three-vertex set lies on a geodesic of length at most two exactly when its part-multiplicity pattern is two plus one. From that characterization, a \((3,2)\)-clique meets at most two parts and uses at most two vertices from each, giving \(2+\min\{2,s\}\), where \(s\) is the number of non-singleton parts. For domination, a two-set in one part dominates exactly when that whole part has order two, while a cross-part two-set dominates exactly in the bipartite case; otherwise two vertices in a part of size at least three plus one outside give a dominating three-set. Independent shortest-path brute force over every complete multipartite type of total order at most nine reproduced both formulas for 87 graph types.
